tasks.title: Carry structured criteria through canonical DoR, ledger, evidence, projections, and approval
criteria: AC1: With empty or unrelated requirement.text, multiple valid structured criteria appear exactly once and in source order in canonical DoR with source identity and target/revision provenance.

AC2: A review using only structured criteria round-trips every criterion exactly once through the canonical ledger, approval evidence, JSON, Markdown, HTML, and inline projections with matching ids, text, status, evidence, and counts.

AC3: A structured criterion that is failed, unproven, or missing valid evidence prevents approval exactly like a text-extracted criterion; pass permits approval only when every other R-0009 gate is satisfied.

AC4: Duplicate, reordered, distinct, empty-text, and malformed mixed-source fixtures prove deterministic identity, order, authoritative provenance, deduplication, and fail-closed rejection without losing distinct criteria.

tasks.title: Enforce explicit-URL and descendant-process no-push isolation at the validation boundary
criteria: AC5: From a registered validation sandbox, git push --no-verify to an explicit URL and refspec returns a stable blocked result and leaves the isolated bare destination bytes and refs unchanged.

AC6: Direct commands plus child, grandchild, shell, package-script, and executable-wrapper processes cannot push via explicit URLs, alternate Git config, --no-verify, or hook overrides, and every block identifies its validation run and sandbox.

AC7: If no-push isolation is unavailable, tampered, or unverifiable, or command cwd escapes the sandbox, dynamic validation does not run and cannot be recorded executed/pass; reviewed checkout and destination refs remain intact.

AC8: Normal read-only builds, tests, dependency reads, and disposable local writes still work in the sandbox; the focused R-0009 dynamic scenario records process-tree isolation evidence and proves original checkout and destination refs unchanged.

tasks.title: Bind lifecycle interception and deduplication to the exact resolved worktree and task identity
criteria: AC10: With a contract active in worktree A, creating a Codex task or running unrelated work bound to worktree B of the same repository is not blocked, replayed, or marked already processed by A; A remains governed and B receives only its own contract.

AC11: Lifecycle deduplication keys include the exact resolved workspace/worktree and task lifecycle identity, so duplicate delivery in one task remains idempotent while identical host event shapes in separate worktrees proceed independently.

tasks.title: Verify both blockers together without changing any other R-0009 behavior
criteria: AC9: Focused tests and the complete R-0009 regression suite pass with no removed, skipped, xfailed, loosened, or reclassified assertion and no change to other R-0009 behavior.
